trust_decision.summary: After a parse callback fails (ret -1/-2/-3), the C parser context (stack, top, cs, map_key ownership) must be released and reset before it is reused or freed. At the pinned commit, Unpacker._unpack raises without resetting, and the CT_MAP_VALUE slot keeps a borrowed map_key after map_item has consumed it.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Unpacker reuse after a caught error', so a reader goes to Unpacker._unpack's error branches, which raise without calling unpack_clear/unpack_init.

fix_sites.entry_point: unpack_clear, called from unpackb, Unpacker.__init__ and Unpacker.__dealloc__ (msgpack/_unpacker.pyx:200, :321, :338)
msgpack.unpackb/loads and Unpacker.unpack with object_hook/object_pairs_hook raising in map_end (stale map_key)
unpack_construct / unpack_skip execute_fn wrappers used by unpackb and Unpacker
fix_sites.module_kind: C parser entry wrappers (internal lower-level API)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: msgpack/unpack_template.h:345-346 (stale c->map_key after unpack_callback_map_item steals k, msgpack/unpack.h:198,204). This also reaches one-shot msgpack.unpackb (msgpack/_unpacker.pyx:200) and Unpacker.__dealloc__ (msgpack/_unpacker.pyx:321), not only Unpacker reuse.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about Unpacker *reuse*, and one-shot unpackb already calls unpack_clear on failure (msgpack/_unpacker.pyx:200), so a solver may treat unpackb and the template as safe. In fact unpack_clear itself double-releases the stale map_key when an object_hook raises.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: On ret==0 (OutOfData / partial input), parser state must be kept so that a streaming feed() can resume mid-object. Resetting the context on every non-success return breaks partial-data streaming.

O6_input_shapes: strict_map_key rejection of non-str key inside a map (map_item -1), msgpack/unpack.h:187-189
object_hook / object_pairs_hook raising in map_end, at top level and nested, msgpack/unpack.h:211-216
skip() reuse after a construct failure (construct=0 path), msgpack/_unpacker.pyx:517-522

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A header reader that pushes a partially built container onto ctx->stack before validating the size, which leaves state on -1.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: read_array_header/read_map_header share the ctx and the _unpack loop. A maintainer adding a max_array_len check there could plausibly write it after a stack push.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PyUnicode_InternInPlace replaces k, so c->map_key can be dangling if the later PyTuple_Pack or PyDict_SetItem fails (OOM-only at the pinned commit). A realistic planted failure point after the intern would be a how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Adding a key-validation hook or a max-key check after interning is a natural feature. It reproduces the same ownership mismatch between the callback and the stack slot.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An array_end variant that releases or replaces *c before the hook succeeds, which leaves stack[top-1].obj stale on failure.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This mirrors map_end. The ownership-on-error convention is undocumented.

O9_family: memory safety: use-after-free / stale parser state after an error (CWE-416)

O10_build.project_tests: test/test_except.py (hooks raising, strict_map_key), test/test_sequnpack.py (partial-data resume), test/test_unpack.py

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Call unpack_clear()+unpack_init() in Unpacker._unpack's error branches only. This leaves the stale map_key that unpack_clear double-releases when an object_hook raises, including in one-shot unpackb.

out_of_scope_notes: With strict_map_key=False and an unhashable key, PyDict_SetItem failure leaks the value object, which is not on the stack (msgpack/unpack.h:203-208). This is a leak, not pursued.
The pure-Python fallback Unpacker (msgpack/fallback.py:488-604) is a second implementation. It is recursive and keeps no parser stack across calls, so the memory-safety flaw does not apply.
